systems.name: West Virginia Public Employees Retirement System

statute.quote: The West Virginia Public Employees Retirement System is hereby created and established to provide for the orderly retirements of employees, of the state and the other participating public employers, who become superannuated because of age or total and permanent disability, and to provide certain survivor benefits.

source.quote: The Consolidated Public Retirement Board is continued to administer all public retirement plans in this state.

website_source.quote: The Public Employees Retirement System (PERS) was established on July 1, 1961 for the purpose of providing retirement benefits for employees of the State and other political subdivisions.

covers_local_source.quote: any political subdivision in the state which has elected to cover its employees, as defined in this article, under the West Virginia Public Employees Retirement System

systems.name: West Virginia Teachers Retirement System

statute.quote: A retirement system to be known as the "state Teachers Retirement System" is hereby established for the purpose of providing retirement allowances for the teachers of West Virginia.

source.quote: The Consolidated Public Retirement Board is continued to administer all public retirement plans in this state.

website_source.quote: The State Teachers' Retirement System (TRS) was established on July 1, 1941 for the purpose of providing retirement benefits for teachers and school service personnel.

covers_local_source.quote: "Employer" means the agency of and within the state which has employed or employs a member, a county board of education which has employed or employs a member, or an electing charter school which has employed or employs a member.

systems.notes: Covers county board of education teachers and school service personnel.

systems.name: West Virginia Deputy Sheriffs Retirement System

statute.quote: There is hereby created the West Virginia Deputy Sheriffs Retirement System.

source.quote: The Consolidated Public Retirement Board is continued to administer all public retirement plans in this state.

website_source.quote: The Deputy Sheriff Retirement System (DSRS), a multiple-employer defined benefit employee retirement system, was established for all deputy sheriffs hired on or after July 1, 1998.

systems.notes: County deputy sheriffs; counties are the employers.

systems.name: West Virginia Emergency Medical Services Retirement System

statute.quote: There is hereby created the West Virginia Emergency Medical Services Retirement System.

source.quote: The Consolidated Public Retirement Board is continued to administer all public retirement plans in this state.

website_source.quote: The Emergency Medical Services Retirement System (EMSRS) was established January 1, 2008 for the purpose of providing retirement benefits for emergency medical services officers employed by participating public employers

covers_local_source.quote: "Participating public employer" means: (1) Any county commission, political subdivision, or county 911 public safety answering point in the state which has elected to cover its emergency medical services officers or 911 personnel

statute.quote: There is hereby established a judges' retirement system for the purpose and to be administered as hereinafter provided.

source.quote: The Consolidated Public Retirement Board is continued to administer all public retirement plans in this state.

website_source.quote: The Judges' Retirement System (JRS) was established on June 5, 1949 for judges and justices of the State of West Virginia who elect to participate in the retirement system.

systems.name: West Virginia Municipal Police Officers and Firefighters Retirement System

statute.quote: There is hereby created the West Virginia Municipal Police Officers and Firefighters Retirement System.

source.quote: The Consolidated Public Retirement Board is continued to administer all public retirement plans in this state.

website_source.quote: The Municipal Police Officers and Firefighters Retirement System (MPFRS) was established January 1, 2010.

covers_local_source.quote: municipal police officer also means an individual employed as a member of a paid police department by a West Virginia municipality or municipal subdivision which is authorized to elect to participate in the plan

systems.name: West Virginia Natural Resources Police Officers Retirement System

statute.quote: There is hereby created the West Virginia Natural Resources Police Officers Retirement System.

source.quote: The Consolidated Public Retirement Board is continued to administer all public retirement plans in this state.

website_source.quote: The Natural Resources Police Officers Retirement System (NRPORS) was established for all Natural Resources Police Officers hired on or after January 2, 2021.

systems.name: West Virginia State Police Death, Disability and Retirement Fund (Plan A)

statute.quote: There is continued the Death, Disability and Retirement Fund created for the benefit of members, retirants and any dependents of retirants or deceased members of the fund.

source.quote: The Consolidated Public Retirement Board is continued to administer all public retirement plans in this state.

website_source.quote: The West Virginia State Police Death, Disability and Retirement Fund, commonly referred to as Plan A, was established for all state troopers on July 1, 1935.

systems.notes: Closed to troopers hired on or after March 12, 1994.

systems.name: West Virginia State Police Retirement System (Plan B)

statute.quote: The West Virginia State Police Retirement System is continued. It is contemplated that substantially all of the members of the retirement system shall be qualified public safety employees as defined in section two of this article.

source.quote: The Consolidated Public Retirement Board is continued to administer all public retirement plans in this state.

website_source.quote: The West Virginia State Police Retirement System, commonly referred to as Plan B, was established by the enactment of Chapter 15, Article 2A of the West Virginia Code during the 1994 Legislative Session for all state troopers hired on or after March 12, 1994.
